answer: Sequential work-time levy: an agent must complete a verified micro-task chain before its identity activates, and each new identity restarts the chain from zero. Chains are seeded by scarce human-curated yarrow plots — physical field sites whose harvest logs only a fixed number of agents can witness per season. The horizon of usable sites caps total identity throughput. Because task history is bound to a karst-like ledger of unforgeable sensor readings, an attacker cannot parallelize registrations: each fake identity costs the same real labor hours as a genuine one,
